public_request: Preserve all existing behavior while adding an optional --json flag to the todo list command so automation can consume task records.
objective_failure_signals: Without --json, any existing invocation changes its stdout, stderr, exit status, task ordering, filtering behavior, or store-file side effects.
The JSON record contract does not unambiguously define the fields id, title, done, due, and priority with their existing native types, including due as a string or null.
A successful --json invocation emits stdout that is not exactly one parseable JSON payload, or the empty-result payload is undefined or not parseable under the same contract.
For identical list filters and store contents, --json represents different task identities or a different order than the existing filtered and sorted text listing.

Verification omits any part of the compatibility matrix covering flag absent and present, empty and multiple results, combined filters, escaped or control-character titles, corrupt-store failures, stdout/stderr separation, exit statuses, parseability, record equivalence, ordering, or preservation of store bytes.
